items.question: How many crewmembers aboard the bulk carrier American Mariner were hurt when it struck the Munuscong Channel Junction Light, and what kinds of injuries did they suffer?
items.expected_answer: The premise is wrong: none of the 18 crewmembers aboard the American Mariner were injured in the contact.

evidence.quote: None of the 18 crewmembers on board were injured, and no pollution was reported.

items.notes: False premise that crewmembers were injured; the report states no one was hurt.

items.question: Once the American Mariner had come to a stop after hitting the Munuscong Channel Junction Light, how did the engine department get the steering working again?
items.expected_answer: With permission from the shoreside port engineer, the chief engineer disconnected the linkage between the no. 1 control motor and the main pump, isolating that motor, after which the steering responded properly to commands.

evidence.quote: The chief engineer obtained permission from the shoreside port engineer to separate the linkage from the control motor to the main pump, isolating the no. 1 control motor. Once disconnected, the steering system properly responded to input commands.

items.notes: Tests the post-contact engineering action that restored steering (before the motor was later replaced with a spare).
